concept: A badge is a status written on the glass as a glyph and a word. Each tone has its own glyph shape in its mark colour, the word is in the text colour, and there is no fill, the same language as Banner (D-018).

root.why: the status in words in the text colour, never colour alone

glyph.why: each tone has its own glyph shape, circle, check, triangle or octagon

dot.why: a neutral status can carry a dot in the secondary colour

info.why: info spends its colour only on the glyph

positive.why: positive spends its colour only on the glyph

warning.why: warning spends its colour only on the glyph

critical.why: critical spends its colour only on the glyph

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop the tone colours, so a real system-colour border keeps the shape

default_to_avoid.pattern: pastel traffic-light pill badges with coloured text (Material badges, every admin template)
default_to_avoid.why_not: tinted fills spend three colours where P1 allows one, and the colour carries the status more than the word does

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: no tinted fill; the tone colour appears only on a small glyph

derivation.consequence: status is spoken in text as well as shown in colour
derivation.form: the status is a word, and each tone has its own glyph shape (circle, check, triangle, octagon)

derivation.consequence: the whole pane is never a hidden button; actions sit on it as separate objects
derivation.form: a badge is a label, not an object to press, so it has no pill to press

derivation.consequence: selected and pressed states change shape or add a mark (a check, a ring), never only colour
derivation.form: the glyph shape differs per tone, so tone survives without colour

options: C glass pill with a glyph
variants.reason: A is Banner's language (D-018) at the size of a word: the glyph carries the colour and the shape, the word carries the meaning (P1, P6). B and C put the glyph in a container, which turns a status into a small object and, in C, into something that looks pressable.
